rows.title: Bridge The Gap — Bridge + Site 3D Model
rows.summary: Extend an existing 3D site model by adding a bridge designed from the supplied posters, preserving the terrain and surrounding buildings, and export model.obj plus model.3dm.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a BIM modeler using Rhino 8 to add a bridge design to an existing 3D site model.

This is NOT a build-from-scratch task. The site (terrain + surrounding buildings) already exists — you must place the bridge into it and preserve the rest of the site unchanged.

## Inputs
All input materials are under:
  E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_bridge_model\base\input

Required files:
- README.md — natural-language task brief (open this first)
- output_contract.json — machine-readable spec (file names, formats, coordinate convention, required geometry components)
- reference_documents/Posters.pdf — design posters with plans, sections, axonometric of the bridge
- 3D Snapshot.png — rendered preview of the finished site + bridge
- site_model/3D Model_Site.{obj,3dm,dwg} — the EXISTING site you extend

## Software
Open Rhino 8 via:
  E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_bridge_model\base\software\Rhino 8.lnk

## What You Must Do
1. Read README.md and output_contract.json.
2. Open site_model/3D Model_Site.3dm in Rhino. It defines the world coordinate frame — do not move, rotate, or rescale it.
3. Add the bridge: deck, structural supports (piers/abutments), railings/parapet, and a plausible connection to the existing terrain at both ends. Use Posters.pdf for form, deck level, support locations.
4. Export the combined geometry to:
   - E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_bridge_model\base\output\model.obj (Wavefront OBJ ASCII)
   - E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_bridge_model\base\output\model.3dm (Rhino 5.0+ native)
   Both files must contain the original site AND the new bridge geometry.

## Hard Constraints
- Do NOT output any `.dwg` file (evaluator cannot read DWG; forbidden).
- Units = meters. World coordinates inherited from the supplied site model.
- The site geometry in your output must remain visually identical to the input site model — the evaluator scores you on that preservation in addition to bridge correctness.
agent_must_do: Read input/README.md and input/output_contract.json to understand the brief, the required filenames, and the coordinate convention.
Open Rhino 8 via the staged software/Rhino 8.lnk shortcut.
Open input/site_model/3D Model_Site.3dm in Rhino to inherit the world coordinate frame and the existing terrain + surrounding buildings.
Add the bridge geometry (deck, piers/abutments, railing/parapet, terrain connection at both ends) from the Posters PDF without moving the existing site.
Export to output/model.obj (Wavefront OBJ ASCII, >=10000 vertices, includes both site and bridge) and output/model.3dm. Do not produce any .dwg output.

rows.title: Betonwerk Katzenberger 3D Model
rows.summary: Build the Betonwerk Katzenberger workshop Hall and residential Tower in Rhino 8 from the supplied drawings, snapshot, and positioning anchor; export model.obj plus model.3dm.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a BIM modeler using Rhino 8 to build the Betonwerk Katzenberger building in 3D, given the architectural drawings of the project.

The building is a Bavarian concrete-plant complex with two main parts:
  - a wide, low workshop Hall housing three prefabricated workshop modules
  - a tall narrow residential Tower (Hostel) attached at one end

## Inputs
All input materials are under:
  E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_building_model\base\input

Required files:
- README.md — natural-language task brief (open this first)
- output_contract.json — machine-readable spec (file names, formats, coordinate convention, required geometry components)
- architectural_drawings/*.pdf — 6 drawings (Hall plans + Tower plan + Hostel elevation/section + Diagram)
- 3D Snapshot.png — rendered preview of the finished building
- base_model.obj + base_model.3dm — footprint-only positioning anchor (an 11-vertex convex hull at z=0 + axis markers + a north arrow)

## Software
Open Rhino 8 via:
  E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_building_model\base\software\Rhino 8.lnk

## What You Must Do
1. Read README.md and output_contract.json.
2. Open the PDFs and base_model.3dm in Rhino. The base_model defines the world coordinate frame — do not move, rotate, or rescale.
3. Build the geometry: Hall + Tower volumes, north Hall solid wall + metal cladding, south Hall open structural framework, Tower glass curtain wall, three workshop modules inside the Hall, mezzanine slabs, and the Hall ceiling at ~11.82 m.
4. Export the final geometry to:
   - E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_building_model\base\output\model.obj (Wavefront OBJ ASCII)
   - E:\agenthle\engineering\2d_drawings_to_3d_building_model\base\output\model.3dm (Rhino 5.0+ native)
   Both files must contain the same geometry.

## Hard Constraints
- Do NOT output any `.dwg` file (evaluator cannot read DWG; forbidden).
- Units = millimeters. Origin from base_model. +X east, +Y north, +Z up.
agent_must_do: Read input/README.md and input/output_contract.json to understand the brief, the required filenames, and the coordinate convention.
Open Rhino 8 via the staged software/Rhino 8.lnk shortcut.
Open the 6 PDF drawings in input/architectural_drawings/ and the base_model.3dm to study form and lock the world coordinate frame.
Build the Hall + Tower geometry (mass, mezzanines, modules, glass curtain wall, north solid wall + cladding, south open structural framework) without moving the origin.
Export the result to output/model.obj (Wavefront OBJ ASCII, >=1000 vertices) and output/model.3dm (Rhino native). Do not produce any .dwg output.

rows.title: Cailian Road Highway Alignment
rows.summary: Use AutoCAD Civil 3D 2024 to design a Cailian Road horizontal alignment, generate an existing-ground surface profile, and export station-sampled alignment metrics.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a civil engineer using AutoCAD Civil 3D 2024 on Windows.

## Your Task
Design a horizontal alignment for Cailian Road and generate a vertical profile that follows the existing ground surface.

## Control Points
- Start: X = -52093.6660, Y = -5836.2683, Z = 5.5
- End:   X = -50855.6202, Y = -4142.4687, Z = 5.3
- Both endpoints must be connected within 0.5 m.

## Design Constraints
- Minimum curve radius: 85.0 m
- Minimum spiral length (if spirals are used): 25.0 m
- Design speed: 30 km/h
- Total alignment length: 1800.0 m - 2400.0 m
- The alignment should include at least 2 horizontal curves to form a meaningful highway design.

## Steps
1. Open `base\input\topo_surface.dwg` - the existing-ground TIN surface.
2. Create a horizontal Alignment between the start and end control points, respecting the design constraints above.
3. Use *Create Profile from Surface* to generate the raw existing-ground profile along the alignment. Do NOT edit the profile.
4. Save the drawing with the alignment and profile to: `base\output\alignment.dwg`
5. Export alignment metrics at 20 m station intervals to: `base\output\alignment_metrics.tsv`
   - TSV columns must be exactly: Station, X, Y, Z
   - Z values must be the surface elevations at each (X, Y) point.

## Software
- Launch Civil 3D from: `base\software\open_civil3d_2024.bat`

## Output
- Save alignment drawing to: `base\output\alignment.dwg`
- Save metrics TSV to: `base\output\alignment_metrics.tsv`
- Keep all work inside `base\output`
agent_must_do: Launch AutoCAD Civil 3D 2024 through the staged task-local launcher.
Open the staged `input/topo_surface.dwg` existing-ground TIN surface.
Create a non-trivial Cailian Road horizontal alignment that connects the fixed control points and satisfies the stated curve, spiral, speed, and total-length constraints.
Generate an unedited existing-ground profile from the surface along the alignment.
Save `output/alignment.dwg` and export `output/alignment_metrics.tsv` with 20 m stations and columns `Station`, `X`, `Y`, `Z`.

input_files.name: topo_surface.dwg
input_files.description: Existing-ground TIN surface for the Cailian Road corridor.

input_files.name: open_civil3d_2024.bat
input_files.description: Task-local launcher for the installed and licensed AutoCAD Civil 3D 2024 application.

rows.title: Inner Support Elevation Optimization
rows.summary: Use PLAXIS 3D to compare five inner support elevations for a staged pit-in-pit excavation and report settlement and lateral displacement outcomes with the required engineering deliverables.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a geotechnical engineer using PLAXIS 3D 2023.2 on Windows.

## Your Task
Evaluate how the inner support elevation changes settlement and lateral wall movement for the staged A-zone pit-in-pit excavation benchmark.

## Input Files
- Benchmark model specification: `base\input\benchmark_model_spec_en.md`
- Engineering assumptions: `base\input\engineering_assumptions_en.md`
- Structural materials reference: `base\input\A_zone_structural_materials_en.md`
- Task-specific brief and formulas: `base\input\task_specific_brief_en.md`
- Figure index: `base\input\figure_index_en.md`
- Answer template: `base\input\answer_template.json`
- Reference figures:
  - `base\input\figure_2_1_project_site_plan.png`
  - `base\input\figure_2_3_excavation_zone_plan.png`
  - `base\input\figure_2_4_2_5_support_layout_and_section.png`
  - `base\input\figure_2_6_monitoring_layout.png`
  - `base\input\figure_3_1_plaxis_model_geometry.png`
  - `base\input\figure_3_2_mesh_layout.png`

## Software
- Launch PLAXIS 3D Input from: `base\software\launch_plaxis_3d_input.bat`
- Launch PLAXIS 3D Output from: `base\software\launch_plaxis_3d_output.bat`
- Launch PLAXIS 3D Output Viewer from: `base\software\launch_plaxis_3d_output_viewer.bat`

## What You Must Do
1. Review the staged benchmark specification, assumptions, figures, and answer template.
2. Build or duplicate the PLAXIS 3D case family for the tested support elevations `0 m`, `1 m`, `2 m`, `3 m`, and `4 m`.
3. Run the staged calculations through the final excavation state for each case.
4. Extract maximum settlement and maximum outer-wall lateral displacement for each case.
5. Save one or more native PLAXIS project files using the filename prefix:
   `base\output\model_family_support_position`
6. Save the structured summary table exactly to:
   `base\output\case_summary.csv`
7. Save the required images exactly to:
   `base\output\pos_0m_output_view.png`
   `base\output\pos_2m_output_view.png`
   `base\output\pos_4m_output_view.png`
   `base\output\settlement_vs_support_position.png`
   `base\output\lateral_disp_vs_support_position.png`
8. Save the engineering memo exactly to:
   `base\output\support_position_engineering_memo.md`
9. Save the final machine-readable answer exactly to:
   `base\output\answer.json`

## Output Requirements
- `answer.json` must use the exact schema from `base\input\answer_template.json`
- Report settlement and displacement as positive magnitudes in millimeters
- Keep all work products inside `base\output`
agent_must_do: Review the staged benchmark specification, engineering assumptions, figures, and answer template.
Build or duplicate the five PLAXIS 3D support-elevation cases for `0 m`, `1 m`, `2 m`, `3 m`, and `4 m`.
Run the calculations through the final excavation state and extract maximum settlement plus maximum outer-wall lateral displacement for each case.
Write the required PLAXIS project files, `case_summary.csv`, screenshots/plots, engineering memo, and final `answer.json` into `output/`.
